12 Platoon, D Company, 1 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
Tanks and infantry from Coral attacked a number of bunker systems in the vicinity of FSPB Coral.

D Coy with tank support returns to the site of B Coy contact of 25 May. An air strike was delivered at  1050hrs. At 1140hrs, D coy with tanks moved into the same area and soon came under RPG, MG and AK47 fire from a well constructed bunker system to hold a coy. The infantry protected the tanks while the latter cleared the jungle with cannister, and blew up or crushed bunkers. Supported by tanks 10 pl kill 3 en.  Contact was halted at  1315hrs but resumed at 1420hrs (GRXT930313) 12 pl joined 10 pl and 14 bunkers were destroyed and at least 3 more en killed. En fired RPG-2 at tanks but had no effect. Aust Inf used flame throwers.

At 1520hrs the action was broken off because of fading light. The force withdrew behind accurate arty and mortar fire. 14 bunkers were destroyed for no loss. Enemy had 7 definitely killed and an unknown number crushed in bunkers. Bunker total was probably closer to 18 but enemy were buried and crushed in their bunkers by tanks. (See Contact Rept from Tanks)

Noted in Combined Arms Data Base

DS POSSUM AND DUSTOFF AC WERE STRUCKBY GROUND FIRE AND FORCED TO LAND. 2 BUSHRANGERS WERE ALSO HIT BY GROUNDFIRE. THE EN FOL UP THE WDR OF 1 PL AND ASLT PNR PL/SP/3RAR AND WOUNDED1 MAN. FOL WDR, LFT CONTINUED TO RECEIVE GROUND FIRE FROM THE CONTACTAREA UNTIL LAST LIGHT. RES: 9 AUST WIA, 2 OF WHOM DOW (INCL 1 RAAF); THEEN SENT OUT FORAGING PARTIES AND RECOVERED THE FOL AUST ARM AND EQPT:1 M60 MG, 3 SLR RIFLES, 1 M79, 30 CLAYMORE MINES, 2 M72, 6LB C4 EXPLOS,4 HE GRENS AND 200 FT OF DET CORD.

See Combined Arms Data Base

1 Platoon A Coy 2RAR/NZ were patrolling when they found a well used track. They followed the track towards the east when the forward scout saw 5 enemy in a group about 10m ahead. The forward section deployed and initiated contact and the 5 enemy were believed to be hit. A second gun group deployed to the right of the forward section. After about 5 minutes the enemy returned heavy fire from the west including AK47s and one 0.30 MG. A short time later intense enemy fire also came from the north and south, pinning the forward section down. The third section made an effort to engage the enemy in this area but was hit severely taking 5 wounded. Arty fire was adjusted as close as was possible to the contact area. Tanks and APCs were assembled and were trying to find a crossing over the Song Rai to join the battle.

Gunships were called and arrived 25 mins later (10min flying time from Nui Dat) and attempted to engage the enemy but had difficulty bringing their fire in close because of difficulties identifying friendly locations and comms difficulties. Several helos were hit by ground fire and two were forced to land. After approx 45 mins, the enemy realised that the Australian platoon was unable to relieve the pressure and began to engage the platoon with a 60mm mortar, RPG 7s and grenades and satchel charges. 2 more Aust casualties resulted. An APC mounted mortar section from 3 RAR commenced firing in support of 1 pl 2 RAR.

After two hours the pls ammo was getting low and the decision was made to attempt to break contact. The dust raised by the enemies explosive weapons enabled the Aust platoon to consolidate its position somewhat and the platoon was able to extract itself from the position using its own firepower to break contact with the enemy. The pls packs and the weapons of the wded were abandoned. Casualties were evacuated under cover of fire and movement by the remainder of the pl and small skirmishes were conducted against groups of enemy attempting to follow up the withdrawal. 1 platoon was relieved by the Assault Pioneer Platoon 3 RAR led by Lt P.J. Abigail. An attempt was set up to evacuate wounded but the helo was hit by en fire resulting in one crewman being wounded (DOW). The attempt was abandoned and the two pls moved towards the Song Rai and the tanks waiting on the other side. One Aust wded had died. The enemy attempted to follow up but was met by the Pnrs and driven off. 1 pnr was wded. The dustoff was effected at 1815hrs. US and Aust gunships continued to attack the enemy until 1900hrs. Arty fired into the area. Pl had clashed with HQ of D445 and C2 Coy.

BODY WAS DRESSED INGREENS AND SANDALS. CREDITED TO 2 RAR/NZ CONTACT AT YS584722 ON 31 MAR. Further body found at YS576716.

units: 5 Platoon, B Company, 3 Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment
notable.report:
5 Platoon, B Coy, 3RAR detected enemy to their front in a suspected bunker system at 061715 hrs. (See Contact Rept). The platoon withdrew and called down artillery fire on the bunker system. Following further artillery and mortar engagement of the target from 0600hrs, the platoon moved forward at 070630 hrs and became engaged in heavy contact with elements of 3/33 Regt. The remainder of B Coy moved to their support. 5 pl advanced with two sections up with rifle grenades ready for use. After moving 200m up a spur 0650hrs a burst of AK47 fire wded one soldier of the left hand section in the throat.  Enemy fire was from a bunker at 15m range. Shortly after another man of the left hand section was wded with GSW to thigh and leg. The right hand section was brought forward on the right flank. It received more enemy fire which included HMGs. 4xM60s were now forward engaging the enemy bunkers. The left hand section wded were evacuated under the fire of the right hand section. A marker balloon was put up at 0745hrs to guide dustoff and Bushranger helos. The first attack by LFT began at 0805hrs. The pl remained under heavy fire despite attacks with miniguns and rockets. At 0845hrs the pl received 3 to 5 rds of RPG. At 0920hrs CHQ joined up with 5 pl and 5 pls low ammo was replenished. The Coy FO went forward to 5 pl and was killed. The heavy firefight continued until it lessened a little at 1000hrs. LFT rocket fire was now reaching to within 30m of 5 pl. At 1045hrs an MG crew received GSW and both were evacuated to the rear. 1105hrs a helo was dropping reserve ammo for the Coy when it was hit by enemy fire and crashed. The pilots and crew were dragged out with ammo beginning to explode from the fire. 2 crew died. At 1200hrs 3xCobra helos relieved the RAAF helos and continued attacks until 1430hrs. At 1500hrs the last enemy fire was received when a member of the left forward section of 5 pl received a GSW while trying to retrieve a weapon.

The bunker system was attacked in rear by 5 Tp C Sqn 1 Armd Regt. Heavy contact continued and 5 Tp was joined by D Coy, 3RAR, 3Tp C Sqn 1 Armd Regt and 2 Tp A Sqn 3 CAV who swept the system and secured it by 071640 hrs (see   ).

Coy OC (Ivan Cahill) noted that smoke grenades had not worked well in marking the coy position for air support. The high canopy (150ft) led to smoke dissipation before it got above the canopy. A smoke gren had to be replenished every minute or two so that position remained marked. By contrast the balloon concept had worked well. Rifle projected grenades had worked well punching through dense vegetation and having good shrapnel effect. M60s proved to be a great problem ( See M60 Machine Gun notes). 3 were brought forward by opdem to replace damaged ones during the fight. There were also other problems with them.

YS420891, ELMS A/3 CAV REGT AND D AND E PL WERE CONTACTED BY ANUNK SIZED FORCE, WHILST PATROLLING IN 3 APC'S. RES: 7 AUST KIA, 3 AUSTWIA FM AN EN INITIATED EXPLOSION.

The section was patrolling along a track when the leading driver saw an artillery illumination cannister which he suspected was part of a mine. He stopped and the enemy opened fire with SA and RPGs. An RPG hit a pile of claymore mines on the back of the last APC which exploded killing the crew and 5 members of the D and E pl wounding 3 others of whom one later died. En was 274 Regt NVA.
